- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.prompt: Search this repository (/bench/repo) for a cron scheduler and any scheduled/cron jobs, especially anything related to database cleanup, nightly jobs, or scheduled tasks. Look for cron expressions, scheduler configuration, job definitions. Report exact file paths and line numbers, and quote the relevant code (job names, schedules/times). I want to know: is there a nightly database-cleanup job? What scheduled jobs exist and at what times? Be thorough — check for cron libraries, scheduler modules, crontab files, etc.

content.text:
I have a complete picture. Here are my findings.

## Summary

There is a fully-implemented, generic cron scheduler package in this repo, but it is **dead code — not wired into the application at all**. There is **no nightly database-cleanup job**. The only real recurring background work is an S3 URL re-presigning task (every 12 hours) and a couple of GitHub Actions crons. No DB-cleanup/prune/purge/retention job exists anywhere.

## 1. The cron scheduler package (`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/`)

A self-contained, GitHub-Actions-inspired cron scheduler with zero external dependencies. Key files:

- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/scheduler.go` — `Scheduler` type, `Register()`, `Start()`, `Stop()`, per-job goroutine loop (`runJobWithSchedule`, lines 121-165).
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/job.go` — `Job` struct (lines 13-36): `Name`, `Schedule` (cron expr), `Timezone`, `Handler`, `Description`, `Tags`.
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/parser.go` — `ParseCronExpression` (line 30) supporting 5-field and 6-field cron, wildcards, ranges, lists, and steps.
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/middleware.go` — logging/recovery/metrics middleware.
- `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/doc.go` — package doc.

Critically, this package is **imported by nothing** outside its own tests. My grep for `internal/scheduler` across all non-test Go files returned no matches, and the only `scheduler.Job{` / `daily-cleanup` reference is inside a doc comment.

The "cleanup" it mentions is only an illustrative example in the docs (`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/doc.go:14-21`):
```go
//	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
//		Name:     "daily-cleanup",
//		Schedule: "0 2 * * *", // 2 AM daily
//		Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
//			// Your cleanup logic here
```
This same example is echoed at `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/job.go:20-21`. There is no actual `daily-cleanup` job implemented or registered.

## 2. Actual scheduled/background work in the running app

Application startup is `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go` → `server.NewServer` → `Server.Start`. The scheduler is never instantiated. The only background runner started is in `/bench/repo/server/server.go`:
- `startBackgroundRunners` (line 153) — creates and runs **only** the S3 presign runner (lines 162-170). No cleanup runner.

**S3 presign runner** — `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`:
- Line 27: `const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` — runs **every 12 hours** (ticker-based, `Run` at line 29). Also runs once immediately at startup (`RunOnce`, server.go:163).
- This is not a cleanup job; it re-presigns S3 attachment URLs before they expire (`CheckAndPresign`, line 47).

## 3. Other periodic (non-cron, non-DB-cleanup) tasks

- `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:199-217` — `cleanupLoop` with `time.NewTicker(CleanupInterval)`; default `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute` (line 60, also `/bench/repo/store/store.go:42`). This evicts expired items from an **in-memory cache only**, not the database.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go:64` — SSE heartbeat ticker (connection keep-alive, not scheduled work).

## 4. GitHub Actions cron schedules

- `/bench/repo/.github/workflows/stale.yml:4-5`:
```yaml
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 */8 * * *" # Every 8 hours
```
This is the GitHub stale-bot for issues/PRs — CI only, unrelated to the database.

No crontab files, docker-compose cron services, or other cron definitions exist in the repo.

## Bottom line
- Nightly database-cleanup job: **No.** None exists.
- Scheduled jobs actually running: the **S3 presign runner every 12 hours** (`s3presign/runner.go:27`) and an in-memory cache eviction loop every 5 minutes (`store/cache/cache.go`).
- The `internal/scheduler` cron package is complete but **unused/dead code**; its "daily-cleanup at 2 AM (`0 2 * * *`)" is only a documentation example.
- CI cron: stale-bot every 8 hours (`0 */8 * * *`) in `.github/workflows/stale.yml`.
